epic.title: compat(ipc): ipcMain/ipcRenderer/contextBridge over host-routed el:<channel> frames, enumerated guard grants and a lifted renderer floor
epic.body:
## Scope
15 entities / 77 members: `ipcMain` (9), `ipcRenderer` (11), `contextBridge` (3), `MessageChannelMain`/`MessagePortMain`, `utilityProcess`/`UtilityProcess`/`parentPort` (→ KEL-75 roles), `IpcMainServiceWorker` (never), `webUtils.getPathForFile`, event structures. Live today: one macOS page-world `window.keld.invoke` (channel 1 only, 4096-byte payload, one pending invoke per WebView, host-minted correlation, isolated-world relay) → `@keld/api` echo handler; no ipcMain, no preload injection, no renderer shim; the Unix VirtualPortRegistry (64-message queue, 4 KiB inline, one-shot transfer) has no renderer route.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites)
draw.io: `ipcRenderer.send`/`on`/`once` + `ipcMain.on` + `event.reply` (15 replies) via one `rendererReq` channel multiplexed by `reqId`; `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` (2 keys); `event.senderFrame.url` read by `validateSender`; `webContents.send` 9. Zettlr: `ipcRenderer.invoke` 186 / `ipcMain.handle` 25, `send` 35, `sendSync` 6 (config store construction), `webContents.send` 49, `event.sender` as a WebContents handle, `webUtils.getPathForFile`, `setMaxListeners(100)`. Zero demand for MessageChannelMain/MessagePortMain/utilityProcess/parentPort/IpcMainServiceWorker.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: all 15 entities exist; never/deferred rows published with denominator honesty.
- L1: draw.io's send/on/once/reply pattern and Zettlr's invoke/handle pattern run on macOS over the lifted floor.
- L2: ordering per channel, error envelope (message-only to the renderer, typed code on the wire), `senderFrame` null-after-navigation, stale-generation reply drop, bounded credit/backpressure pass pinned conformance entries.
- L3: corpus apps' IPC workflows pass under `keld dev` with facade-overhead measured (X05).

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-80 (bounded virtual channels: N-pending credit window, host→renderer events — the floor v2), KEL-142 (bridge seam), KEL-136 (transport), KEL-75 (virtual ports, roles), KEL-102 (guard dispatch), SCV codec owner (F03-D4, open), `windows.<w>.channels` grant vocabulary spec (open, no owner today).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters + panel)
- Carriage: one fixed, generated kipc control channel per direction for the compat namespace; the Electron channel string, a kind discriminator (event | invoke | sync | ports) and the SCV bytes are payload fields; the host matches the channel string against the per-window enumerated `el:<channel>` grant (`KELD-GUARD003` on miss) and forwards opaque bytes. No runtime-minted u16 ids.
- The renderer→main authorization boundary is the enumerated per-window channel grant, not the preload (both corpus preloads expose arbitrary-channel send/invoke to the page); `keld migrate` emits enumerated grants from static analysis and refuses `el:*`.
- The live KEL-142 floor cannot carry either corpus app; floor v2 (KEL-80 slice) = (a) N pending invokes per WebView under a host-enforced credit window, (b) `window.keld.send` + `window.keld.on` host→renderer events, (c) payload bound raised by measurement (draw.io ships base64 PNG exports through IPC).
- `event.sender` = facade WebContents keyed by host webview id; `event.senderFrame.url` host-minted and null after navigation; `event.reply` binds to the sender document generation (survives same-document hash changes, as Electron keys on the frame host); stale replies are dropped silently like Electron.
- `ipcMain.handle` errors reach the renderer as the message only; the typed `KELD-*` code stays on the wire and in diagnostics.
- `sendSync` must remain a blocking CALL with deadline, rate limit and dev warning (arch 02 §5, KEL-127); it is SCAFFOLDED (typed throw + fix-it to invoke) until the WKWebView synchronous-XHR experiment passes (Zettlr-gated, 0 draw.io sites).
- MessageChannelMain/MessagePortMain/utilityProcess/parentPort are deferred behind zero demand and KEL-75 AC7 (pinned-oracle fixture first); IpcMainServiceWorker/exposeInIsolatedWorld/executeInMainWorld are documented ✘.

decision_tickets.title: Who owns the `windows.<w>.channels` grant vocabulary and its evaluator (no live evaluator exists; KEL-102 and KEL-80 do not own it)?
decision_tickets.question: The per-window enumerated `el:<channel>` grant is the renderer→main authorization boundary (panel consensus), but `evaluate` reads only `manifest.app` today and the MCP explain tool refuses `channel`. An approved arch 03 §2 amendment with a named owner is required; the `el:*` example in arch 03 §3 must be revised in the same PR (code/spec mismatch rule).

decision_tickets.title: Synchronous cross-world function calls: can a contextBridge-exposed function return a value synchronously on WKWebView/WebKitGTK worlds?
decision_tickets.question: Zettlr exposes functions whose page-visible return is produced synchronously (config.get via sendSync wrapper). Both worlds share the DOM, so a shared-DOM relay is a lead; unverified. Measure a cross-world relay (per-call cost, sync return feasibility) in the KEL-142 fixture; fallback is async-only exposure (▲) which keeps draw.io config-only.

decision_tickets.title: One navigation-generation owner: unify the bridge counter and the guard webview generation
decision_tickets.question: Two generation counters exist today (bridge navigation generation rotated on navigation start; guard Principal::Webview.generation). senderFrame/reply/stale-reply semantics need exactly one owner minted by the host window registry. Decide the owner and the rotation point (navigation commit vs start).

decision_tickets.title: Renderer sendSync mechanism on WKWebView (synchronous XHR to a host scheme handler) — measured feasibility
decision_tickets.question: Arch 02 §5 and KEL-127 require sendSync to exist as a blocking CALL with deadline, rate limit and dev warning; no engine-portable blocking primitive is known on WKWebView. Experiment: page issues a synchronous XMLHttpRequest to a WKURLSchemeHandler-backed scheme that forwards to a stub reply; record thread behaviour, stall, RTT and deadline; derive the rate limit. Zettlr-gated (6 sites); draw.io has 0.

ambiguity_laundering.claim: 'Design facts fixed by research: Preload runs in a dedicated app content world (third world), not the trusted KEL-142 world.'
ambiguity_laundering.problem: PANEL-D21 is published as CONTESTED and open ('the world choice is open ... decide on arm G results and measured relay cost, not prose') and gates F04-T4 and F07-T1. A contested decision is presented as a fixed fact; F07-T1 even lists a 'KEL-142 spec revision (third world/relay)' predecessor.
ambiguity_laundering.fix: INFERENCE (one invariants refuter): co-locating the preload with the KEL-142 handler/nonce is unsafe, so a third world is the leading candidate. UNKNOWN until PANEL-D21 arm G: same-world-with-proxy vs third world, and the relay's per-call cost.

ambiguity_laundering.claim: 'draw.io Desktop ... uses app, BrowserWindow, ..., nativeTheme, `<webview>`, electron-updater ...' and 'Zettlr ... 187 `invoke` call sites'.
ambiguity_laundering.problem: Contradicts the plan's own corrected facts: draw.io disables <webview> everywhere (webviewTag:false at :728/:1090/:1407/:2210/:3087; will-attach-webview preventDefault at :2223), and F04-EPIC/PANEL-D15/the briefing count 186 invoke sites. Token-scan output survived as a usage statement.
ambiguity_laundering.fix: 'draw.io sets webviewTag:false on every window and vetoes will-attach-webview (zero <webview> use)'; 'Zettlr: 186 ipcRenderer.invoke call sites (resolved)'.

ambiguity_laundering.claim: 'event.reply binds to the sender document generation (survives same-document hash changes, as Electron keys on the frame host); stale replies are dropped silently like Electron.'
ambiguity_laundering.problem: Stated as a design fact with no v44.4.5 receipt, while the MAP's forbidden-claims list bans exactly this class of sentence ('webContents.send is dropped after navigation'). The F04 invariants refuter also showed the premise 'Keld rotates Principal::Webview.generation on navigation' is false today (live backends mint generation 0; the bridge keeps a separate u64).
ambiguity_laundering.fix: FACT (doc, as cited in F04-T1): senderFrame may be null after the frame navigated or was destroyed. INFERENCE: reply-after-navigation is dropped silently in Electron — needs a source receipt or a recorded fixture. FACT: Keld has two counters today; the binding rule is undecided (F04-A4).

ambiguity_laundering.claim: 'Lift the KEL-142 floor as the first KEL-80 slice' / 'KEL-80 (owner; product-spine subset per GitHub #323)'.

decision_packets.decision: Which single owner mints the navigation generation consumed by the bridge, the guard webview principal and senderFrame/reply semantics, and at which point it rotates.
facts: The bridge keeps a private `navigation_generation: u64` per WebView, stamps it on every admitted renderer request (documented there as the 'host-owned navigation generation that admitted this call') and settles replies only for the matching generation (crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs, origin/main b4b907c3).
That counter rotates in two places: when the host calls the engine's navigate, and on wry `PageLoadEvent::Started` (crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/mod.rs).

wry 0.56.1 (the Cargo.lock pin) emits `PageLoadEvent::Started` from WKNavigationDelegate `webView:didCommitNavigation:` (wry-0.56.1 src/wkwebview/navigation.rs). So engine-observed rotation is at commit, not provisional start, and one host-initiated navigation rotates twice.
The guard principal is `Principal::Webview { id, generation: u32 }`; live media backends mint generation 0 (crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs; crates/keld-wv/src/media.rs WEBVIEW_MEDIA_GENERATION).

The approved KEL-102 spec says the webview caller is 'created and rotated only by the host webview/navigation registry' and 'Current backends use generation 0; a later navigation registry must increment it before a post-navigation request can dispatch' (docs/specs/kel102-host-guard-enforcement.md lines 399, 414-416).

The KEL-142 spec binds the document nonce to `(WebviewId, navigation generation)` and requires that 'provisional/new navigation invalidates the previous nonce before the new document may dispatch' (docs/specs/kel142-macos-renderer-bridge-api.md §5.2 items 3 and 6). It does not pin an integer width.
Neither the KEL-142 nor the KEL-139 spec, nor the bridge code, mentions same-document navigation (grep for same-document/hashchange/fragment/pushState, 2026-10-06).

draw.io checks `event.senderFrame` in `validateSender` (null means reject, otherwise URL prefix match) before acting on renderer messages, and replies with `event.reply` (corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb src/main/electron.js).
KEL-102 is In Progress, KEL-142 is Done, KEL-143 is Backlog (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06).
inferences: The ticket's premise 'rotated on navigation start' is only half right: for renderer-initiated navigations the live rotation is at commit, which already matches Electron's frame-bound reply semantics and leaves a cancelled provisional navigation's document usable.

Because the first proof dispatches renderer channels under a webview principal (F04-A1), the KEL-102 sentence forbids doing so with a constant generation 0; unification is therefore a first-proof requirement, not polish.
WKWebView does not call didCommitNavigation for same-document (fragment/history) navigations, so the live code probably does not rotate on a hash change; this is unverified.
A new keld-core registry type is not needed for the first proof: one live mint already exists and already travels with each request.
unknowns: Whether a same-document navigation on WKWebView triggers the commit callback (would drop replies Electron delivers).
Whether a host-initiated load that fails before commit leaves the previous document with an invalidated nonce and no way to re-bind.
Whether the populated draw.io webapp mutates `location.hash` during the 4-step workflow.

The existing per-WebView host navigation state is the single mint; the guard webview principal for channel dispatch is built from the generation stamped on the admitted request, never from a constant. Rotation: cross-document commit, plus host-initiated load request as an earlier fail-closed invalidation; never on same-document navigation. alternatives.new_invariant: For any dispatched renderer request, the generation that admitted it, the generation in the guard principal and the generation deciding senderFrame nullability and reply delivery are the same value from one mint.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142's public request accessor type changes (public-API gate on keld-wv); the media path keeps constant 0 until KEL-102's media unit adopts the same source, which must be recorded as a named residual.

alternatives.option: B. Lift the counter into a new keld-core window/webview registry now and make both the bridge and the guard consume it.
alternatives.cost: A new registry type and a cross-crate callback from the engine page-load handler, built for one live WebView.
alternatives.new_invariant: keld-core owns all webview identity state.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: YAGNI for the first proof; risk of an unexercised abstraction. This remains the destination when a second consumer (media rotation, multiple webviews) needs it.

alternatives.option: C. Keep two counters and document a mapping.
alternatives.cost: None now.
alternatives.new_invariant: None.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: One rule, one owner; senderFrame nullability and guard revocation can disagree. Rejected.

alternatives.option: D. Rotate at provisional start for all navigations.
alternatives.cost: Engine delegate work to observe provisional start.
alternatives.new_invariant: Earlier invalidation.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: A cancelled navigation (draw.io prevents navigations) would strand the live document without a bridge; diverges from Electron, which keeps the old frame until commit. Rejected.
